gap: No result ChatGPT got states cost per USB-C watt or watts per ounce for current adapters. Worked out from TESSAN's own store today, the TESSAN WTA09 gives a 65 W laptop port for $0.43 per watt ($27.99 ÷ 65 W). The Voyager 205 has the most output for its weight at 17.3 W/oz, and the 20–25 W 'ultra thin' adapters cost more than $1 per watt.
standout_why: I compared four pages. Pack & Porter lists a weight (5.1 oz), ~30 W shared output and $17.99 for the EPICKA TA-105C, but works out no ratio and says no product's per-port split is published. NBC Select gives prices and USB wattage but no weights. The Finer Route gives wattage and ports but no prices or weights. The product title on the Ceptics page from ChatGPT's results only lists USB-A + USB-C. None of these pages has watts per ounce or price per USB-C watt for any product.
decides: For a shopper bringing a USB-C laptop, the ratio points to the TESSAN WTA09 ($27.99, 65 W, $0.43/W) over the Epicka TA-105S ChatGPT showed (45 W at $24.99 is $0.56/W, but that price is from ChatGPT's card, not a page I opened). If weight matters more than price, the WTA07 gives the same 65 W in 6.04 oz instead of 7.18 oz, for $15 more. For phone-only travel in Type C countries, the Ceptics CTU-9C is $9.99 for one unit on Ceptics' site today. The $17.99 ChatGPT showed matches the two-adapter CTU-9-9C Europe combo, so the shopper was shown nearly double the single-adapter price.
